content.text: I have everything needed: the file itself, its callee `gitAuthArgs`, the config, the sole caller `registerRepo`, and `package.json` (no test suite exists). No further reads are required.

input.reason: src/routes.ts:19-22 takes `remoteUrl` from `req.body`, checks only that it is non-empty, and passes it to `cloneRepo`. src/worktree.ts:15 calls `gitAuthArgs(repo.remoteUrl, SERVICE_TOKEN)` and spreads the result into the `git clone` argv. src/git-auth.ts:7-12 attaches `http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer ${token}` whenever `remoteUrl.includes("github.com")` is true and returns `[]` otherwise. That substring check refutes the finding's "whatever host the URL names" wording (e.g. `https://evil.example/repo` gets no header), but it is trivially satisfied by attacker hosts such as `https://github.com.evil.example/repo` or any URL with `github.com` in its path, so the central claim that the service token is sent to a user-chosen host holds. There are no tests in the repository (package.json has only `node --test` with no test files) and no other validation of `remoteUrl`.
input.summary: cloneRepo leaks service token to any host whose URL contains github.com

findings.text: `cloneRepo` passes the user-supplied `remoteUrl` straight to `gitAuthArgs` with the service token, so `git clone` sends the token to any host named by a URL containing the substring `github.com`.
findings.reason: The first clause holds: routes.ts:19-22 forwards `req.body.remoteUrl` with only a truthiness check, and worktree.ts:15 passes it to `gitAuthArgs(repo.remoteUrl, SERVICE_TOKEN)`. The consequence clause overreaches: git-auth.ts:8-11 returns `[]` unless `remoteUrl.includes("github.com")`, so a URL like `https://evil.example/repo` receives no Authorization header. Because the check is a substring match rather than a host check, URLs such as `https://github.com.evil.example/repo` or `https://evil.example/github.com` still receive the token, so the leak is real; the text is narrowed to the condition the code actually imposes.

input.severity_reason: Any authenticated user can call `registerRepo` with a URL such as `https://github.com.attacker.example/x`; the only guard is a substring match on `github.com` (git-auth.ts:8), after which `git clone` sends `Authorization: Bearer <HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN>` to the attacker's server. This is a directly exploitable exfiltration of the service credential.
